prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active forms that made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B046 alone, with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange tested it from several directions and the scientific case held. The discovery chain (proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, glucose-dependent insulin secretion, central and gastric effects on appetite) is physiological in the strict sense, it has been confirmed independently for decades, and it has led to treatments with cardiovascular and renal benefit in large outcome trials. Maturity is not in question. Unanimity among the six of us is not part of my argument. What I take from the exchange is that every member located the weakness in attribution and not in merit, which is the right place to look. A single-part prize is also the cleanest use of the three-person cap, since a second part would force a reduction of the physiology trio and would weaken the part that carries the strongest case.
statement.case_against: The reservation I stated in round 1 stands. Four credited names become three, Knudsen's long-acting analogues are what reached patients, and Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to Habener's group, who are not credited, is contested and cannot be settled from the supplied record. A physiology citation can be read as skipping the step that made the medicine, and a citation that includes drug development can be read as honouring industrial optimisation. I now think this is best managed in the citation wording and not by changing names: the citation should name the physiology of GLP-1 and its active forms and state the therapeutic consequence, without claiming priority for any one group on the active peptide. I would also record in our deliberations that Habener and the early proglucagon sequencing groups are a limit of the supplied credit. I cannot show that this limit changes the configuration, and I have not changed my position because of it.

responses.point: Chose the physiology reading over the drug-development reading and accepted that this choice is not uncontroversial, arguing that folding in Knudsen risks crediting an industrial optimisation step instead of a discovery.
responses.response: I now agree with this more than I stated in round 1, where I described a Mojsov-for-Knudsen swap as the fallback if the committee treats development as essential. Your point is the stronger one. Long-acting analogue design builds on the physiology and does not add a new biological finding, and a swap would trade a contested priority claim for a category question about what the prize rewards. I keep the swap as a fallback only if the committee decides that Mojsov's priority is not defensible, and not because the product matters more than the discovery. Where I still differ is the cost. Leaving Knudsen out has to be stated openly as a limit of the three-person cap and not presented as a clean line between discovery and engineering.

responses.point: Would keep Mojsov for identification and synthesis of the active peptide, and named Holst and Drucker alone as a thinner but defensible fallback. Also raised the missing chimeric-receptor originator (Eshhar) as a defect in B040.
responses.response: On B046 I side with keeping Mojsov. Dropping her to a pair would remove the identification and synthesis of the active peptide from a discovery chain whose logic depends on it, and the priority dispute with Habener is a reason for careful citation wording, not for removing a name whose contribution is documented. I accept that a Holst and Drucker pair is defensible, but it is a worse description of the discovery. On B040 I share the concern about Eshhar. It is the main reason I would not move CAR-T above GLP-1, and it also means that if the committee ever advances B040, the attribution problem is larger than the June and Sadelain versus Rosenberg question we discussed in round 1.

responses.point: Said a second part would require reducing the B046 trio because of the three-person cap, and listed B031 as an alternative, together with B040.
responses.response: I agree on the cap, and it is the practical reason I do not support a second part. Pairing B040 with B046 would take at least one name from the GLP-1 trio, and I do not see which of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov can be spared. On B031 I move toward your view. Mori and Walter are the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and I replace B049 with B031 as my second alternative. Optogenetics still has the six-name problem, which no three-person cut resolves in a principled way. My earlier point about the translational immaturity of the unfolded protein response is a reason to rank it below B046 this year, not a reason to say it will never be eligible.

responses.point: Argued that precedent supports honouring enabling methods, which is the basis for B049 as an alternative, and raised the unresolved question of which second achievement could share the prize without displacing a GLP-1 laureate.
responses.response: I take the precedent for methods seriously, and I agree that no second part is currently possible without displacing a GLP-1 name. That is why I come to a different conclusion from yours on B049 and not because I discount its originality. The channel discovery by Nagel and Hegemann and the neuronal deployment are both decisive, and cutting three of six is the sort of exclusion that would be criticised more than the Knudsen exclusion. Given that, I put B049 below B031 as a fallback. I would reconsider only if the committee found a principled three-person basis, for example the channel discovery alone, which I do not think the record supports at present.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide can be defended against Habener's group; if the committee finds it cannot, I would replace her with Knudsen and not drop to a pair.
Whether the citation can credit the therapeutic consequence without implying that drug development was the discovery.
Whether Habener and the early proglucagon sequencing groups, outside the supplied credit, should be recorded in our deliberations as a limit of the attribution.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. I have no documented co-authorship with the credited names on B046, B040 or B031, and I do not infer ties from shared institutions. My field is autoimmunity and Ro52/TRIM21, and none of the shortlisted candidates falls in it. The TNF blockade work (B044), which is close to my field, is not on the shortlist. I have read the other members' disclosures. Those between Perlmann, Svenningsson and El-Manira, and those between Linnarsson and Sandberg, do not affect my own position.
